memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "I am going to bring floodwaters on the earth to destroy all life under the heavens, every creature that has the breath of life in it. Everything on earth will perish. But I will establish my covenant with you, and you will enter the ark - you and your sons and your wife and your sons' wives with you." - Gen 6:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Again we hear that word of hope: but. "Everything on earth will perish. But I will establish my covenant with you." In the midst of announcing total judgement, God makes a promise - a covenant - to Noah and his family. Here, for the first time in the Bible, God speaks of establishing a covenant, a binding relationship of committed love and faithfulness.

This is the heart of how God relates to His people throughout Scripture - not through fear alone, but through covenant. He binds Himself in faithful promise to save and keep those who are His. And notice the sweep of grace: the covenant includes Noah's whole family. God's saving purpose reaches beyond the individual to bless households and generations.

Noah's part was simply to "enter the ark" - to take God at His word and step inside the rescue God provided. Salvation was offered; it had to be entered by faith.

This covenant with Noah is one thread in the great tapestry of God's saving promises that reaches its climax in Christ. Jesus, on the night before He died, spoke of "the new covenant in my blood" (Luke 22:20) - God's ultimate, unbreakable promise to save all who come to Him. The God who covenanted to rescue Noah has covenanted to rescue you in Christ. Enter in, and trust His promise.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you rest in God's covenant promise to save those who trust Him?
- Are you praying for your whole household to be saved?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, thank You that You bind Yourself in covenant to rescue those who trust You. Thank You for the new covenant in Jesus' blood. I enter in and rest in Your promise, and I pray for my whole family.
